title: A Regiment for the Lantern
premise: In the winter of 1919, in a river town still smoldering from the war, Marguerite Winterbourne secretly completes the atlas her murdered master died protecting — an atlas whose final plates chart fortifications the armistice commission was never meant to see. When the season's floods close the only bridge, she is trapped with Captain Elias Voss, the occupying officer her master once promised safe passage to, now declared an enemy deserter with a bounty on his head. Marguerite must choose between delivering the atlas that will secure her own future and honoring a peacetime promise that could hang them both. In the end she burns the incriminating plates, ferries Voss across the flooded river by lantern light, and signs the finished atlas with both their names.
about_author: Lior Ishikawa is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border maps from postwar Europe. They write historical fiction about the people who draw lines on paper and the people who die for them.

chapters.title: The Ink That Would Not Dry
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She works late finishing the atlas in her dead master's studio, hiding the final fortification plates beneath floorboards when the town garrison comes asking questions. Emotional beat: grief braided with fear; she realizes the atlas is both inheritance and indictment.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to 1914. She recalls her master swearing an oath of safe passage to young Lieutenant Voss before the borders closed. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited debt — promises outliving the men who made them.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Floodwaters take the bridge; the town seals itself for the season. That night she finds Voss wounded in the chapel crypt, seeking the passage her master promised. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant compassion as she takes him in.

chapters.title: What the Commission Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He reveals the armistice commission is coming to audit the town's records — and that her master was killed because of the atlas. He offers testimony in exchange for passage. Emotional beat: wary negotiation between two people who need each other and trust nothing.

chapters.title: Neighbors, Informants
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The garrison posts a reward for the deserter; her friend Odette begins asking pointed questions about lights in the studio at night. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a vise; loyalty tested in small daily betrayals.

chapters.title: The Plates Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He discovers the hidden fortification plates and realizes Marguerite has been sitting on the very evidence that could condemn or save hundreds. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into understanding — she was protecting the town, not hoarding power.

chapters.title: Odette's Choice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Odette discovers Voss and must decide whether to report him; instead she brings medicine and a warning: the commission arrives in three days. Emotional beat: unexpected solidarity among women who have all lost something to the war.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The commission arrives; Marguerite presents the atlas with forged plates substituted while Voss hides in plain sight as a hired porter. A sharp-eyed commissioner lingers over one inconsistency. Emotional beat: sustained terror of the near-miss, and the intoxication of getting away with it.

chapters.title: Lantern Light on Black Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The commissioner returns at night; Odette covers their escape as Marguerite and Voss cross the flood by rowboat, burning the true plates mid-river so no one can ever use them. Emotional beat: the climax — sacrifice of ambition and truth for mercy, paid in fire on water.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Title Page
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue in spring. The bridge reopens; the atlas is published under her master's name alone, but she inscribes both names on the dedication page kept in her private copy. Voss sends a letter from across the border. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — survival's price paid, loyalty honored, truth kept where it can do no harm.
